title: What If China Nuked a US Ally After 6 Days of War?
description:
What happens if the US and China run out of missiles in a Pacific war, and then one nuclear weapon is used?

In this simulation, one 5-kiloton nuke bursts over a small island on day 6 of a US-China war, after the American anti-ship missile runs dry on day 4.

Eleven twenty-six, Batan Island. A single DF-26 missile flies six minutes and the first nuclear weapon used in war since Nagasaki bursts over a small airport in the Luzon Strait. Which side runs short of missiles first, and does it still matter? Before the simulation we look at what is real: the missiles the Iran war used up, the CSIS wargame where the key anti-ship round ran out in three to seven days, and how slowly the stocks are rebuilt.

This is a simulation. It has not happened. The salvos, the launch sites, the day, the target and the yield are fictional design choices built from published models and open sources, not predictions of any government's policy, and tied to no real date.

- CSIS wargame results, Conflict in the Western Pacific and the Defense Industrial Base (2023): https://chinaselectcommittee.house.gov/sites/evo-subsites/selectcommitteeontheccp.house.gov/files/evo-media-document/CSIS%20Simulation%20Results.pdf
- Pentagon, Military and Security Developments Involving the PRC (2025): https://media.defense.gov/2025/Dec/23/2003849070/-1/-1/1/ANNUAL-REPORT-TO-CONGRESS-MILITARY-AND-SECURITY-DEVELOPMENTS-INVOLVING-THE-PEOPLES-REPUBLIC-OF-CHINA-2025.PDF

Missile counts are outside estimates; real inventories are classified. Blast and burn figures: Glasstone and Dolan, The Effects of Nuclear Weapons (1977), calibrated to NUKEMAP by Alex Wellerstein.

How this video was made: the narration is AI-generated (Google Text-to-Speech). Scenario segments are simulations built from published models and open sources; the salvos, the day, the target, the yield and the wind are ours, a scenario, not a forecast.
Maps: Natural Earth (public domain), OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL) via OpenFreeMap and OpenMapTiles. Music: generated with Eleven Music.
